st: Forcing yourself to do just one thing, against generative art and constant distraction

sec.p: The anxiety of our digital society is fuelled by FOMO, fear of missing out. During COVID, I remember living on Reddit's r/covid page, refreshing it to track infection data for every micro-region on the planet and find out the latest R0.

Analogue was simpler. As a kid, I'd buy a CD (for the price of a month of Spotify) and wring it dry for months in the car. I subscribed to Internazionale, which I read, distraction-free, cover to cover.

sec.t: ff.72.3 If the Library of Alexandria had 100 books
sec.p: Too many books? According to Naval, yes (from the podcast mentioned here: 🎁 ff.68.4 Less ego and control, more flow and presence: Naval's cure). So much so that people end up reading dozens of personal finance books without ever leafing through Adam Smith's The Wealth of…

sec.t: ff.72.4 From multitasking to the Greek classics (and arete)
sec.p: As with books and CDs, we need to extend the philosophy of ONE to our whole being: one screen, one tab, one activity, one thought.
